argument.claim: Even a more accurate AI would not remove the core objection: decisions to kill need meaningful human judgment and a responsible human.
argument.logic_line: Because autonomous killing creates a responsibility gap (S1), humans in the loop drift into rubber-stamping (S2), and greater distance makes war easier to start (S3), accuracy alone cannot justify removing human judgment.
supports: Responsibility gap: when a machine selects a target, no one may be fully answerable.
Automation bias: people formally in the loop defer to the system.
Distance lowers the threshold for war.
argument.counterclaim_response: Concede democratic authority for limits in law; distinguish decision support from delegated kill decisions; rebut neutrality.

sources.text: philosopher Robert Sparrow's Killer Robots (2007) argues that just war requires someone who can be held responsible for each death.
the case warns that a human may remain in the loop but rely on the system, and that a well-timed suggestion can steer a decision.
